catalyst_text: Reported positive preliminary Phase 1 monotherapy data
detailed_catalyst_text: Initial U.S. Phase 1 monotherapy data in KRAS-mutant solid tumors showed favorable safety and tolerability with no treatment-related discontinuations and encouraging pharmacokinetics. Preliminary antitumor activity was observed, supporting combination potential with the pan-RAS agent. These data support continued dose escalation and combination development.
catalyst_text_evidence: The Company also announced encouraging initial U.S. Phase 1 monotherapy data for potential first-in-class pan-KRAS inhibitor ERAS-4001, supporting its combination potential with ERAS-0015. Favorable safety and tolerability data with predominantly low-grade adverse events and no TRAEs leading to treatment discontinuation Pharmacokinetic (PK) results were encouraging and support continued dose escalation Preliminary monotherapy antitumor activity supports ERAS-4001’s potential as a combination partner for ERAS-0015.

catalyst_text: Reported positive Phase 1 monotherapy efficacy in NSCLC
detailed_catalyst_text: Updated Phase 1 monotherapy data in KRAS-mutant NSCLC showed 60% confirmed ORR at 32 mg QD in 2L/3L patients previously treated with an immune checkpoint inhibitor and platinum chemotherapy, with activity across G12D and G12V subtypes. All responders and patients with stable disease at 32 mg remained on treatment. These findings support continued development in lung cancer.
catalyst_text_evidence: KRAS G12X non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) 60% confirmed ORR (N=5) at 32 mg QD and 58% confirmed ORR (N=12) across the PAD range of 16-32 mg QD in the 2L or 3L setting following an immune checkpoint inhibitor and platinum-based chemotherapy (post-ICI/platinum) Activity was observed across multiple KRAS mutation subtypes at 32 mg QD in the 2L+ setting: 60% confirmed ORR (N=5) in patients with KRAS G12D mutations 50% confirmed ORR (N=4) in patients with KRAS G12V mutations At 32 mg QD in the 2L+ setting, all (5 of 5) patients with confirmed responses and all (5 of 5) patients with stable disease remained on treatment.

catalyst_text: Reported positive Phase 1 combination tolerability and responses
detailed_catalyst_text: Early Phase 1 combination with pembrolizumab showed favorable tolerability with no DLTs through the 32 mg QD cohort. Multiple responses were observed across multiple solid tumor types in dose escalation. Results support advancing immunotherapy combinations.
catalyst_text_evidence: ERAS-0015 plus pembrolizumab: Generally well tolerated with favorable safety data and no unexpected safety signals The DLT window was cleared through the 32 mg QD ERAS-0015 cohort with no DLTs Multiple responses observed in multiple solid tumor types in dose escalation.

catalyst_text: Announced positive Phase 1 efficacy in biliary cancer
detailed_catalyst_text: Initial Phase 1 monotherapy results in KRAS-mutant biliary tract cancer at 32 mg QD in the 1L+ setting showed a 75% confirmed ORR (N=4). All responders remained on treatment. These findings suggest promising activity in this hard-to-treat population.
catalyst_text_evidence: KRAS G12X biliary tract cancer (BTC) at 32 mg QD in the 1L+ setting 75% confirmed ORR (N=4) All (3 of 3) patients with confirmed responses remained on treatment.

catalyst_text: Reported positive Phase 1 monotherapy and combination data
detailed_catalyst_text: Updated U.S. Phase 1 results showed strong monotherapy activity in KRAS-mutant pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma at 32 mg QD, with 44% confirmed ORR overall and 69% in G12D/V subtypes in a heavily pretreated 2L+ population. Early combination with gemcitabine plus nab-paclitaxel was generally well tolerated with no DLTs through 16 mg, supporting further development in 1L PDAC. These data indicate meaningful efficacy and favorable tolerability supporting advancement.
catalyst_text_evidence: Erasca, Inc. ... today announced positive updated U.S. Phase 1 monotherapy and initial combination data reinforcing the best-in-class potential of pan-RAS molecular glue ERAS-0015 in patients with RAS-mutant solid tumors. KRAS G12X pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) at 32 mg QD in the second-line or greater (2L+) setting 44% confirmed objective response rate (ORR) across all patients (N=25) with KRAS G12X mutations; 84% were treated in the third-line or later (3L+) setting and 44% had G12R mutations 69% confirmed ORR in patients (N=13) with KRAS G12D or G12V PDAC, which represent nearly 70% of patients with PDAC. Of these patients, 77% were treated in 3L+ All (11 of 11) patients with confirmed responses and 6 of 11 patients with stable disease remained on treatment. ERAS-0015 plus gemcitabine + nab-paclitaxel (Days 1 and 15): Generally well tolerated with favorable safety data and no unexpected safety signals The DLT window was cleared through the 16 mg QD ERAS-0015 cohort with no DLTs Efficacy data not yet available Clinical data support further development in 1L PDAC.

catalyst_text: Reported positive Phase 1 combination efficacy signals
detailed_catalyst_text: Early Phase 1 combination with panitumumab in KRAS-mutant colorectal cancer was generally well tolerated. Multiple responses were seen, including two ongoing confirmed partial responses and one unconfirmed partial response across 16–24 mg cohorts. These signals warrant continued evaluation.
catalyst_text_evidence: ERAS-0015 plus panitumumab: 16 mg QD ERAS-0015 was generally well tolerated with favorable safety data and no unexpected safety signals Multiple responses were observed in dose escalation in patients with KRAS G12X colorectal cancer (CRC), including 2 ongoing confirmed partial responses (PR) in 2 patients treated at 24 mg QD who then dose reduced to 16 mg QD, and 1 unconfirmed PR (uPR) in 4 patients treated at 16 mg QD.

drug_indication: Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma, Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer
catalyst_text: Announced Phase 1/2 trial opened for enrollment
detailed_catalyst_text: A Phase 1/2 open-label, multicenter trial evaluating vopimetostat in combination with ERAS-0015 is now open for enrollment in MTAP-deleted pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma and MTAP-deleted/RAS-mutant non-small cell lung cancer. This trial initiation marks the start of clinical testing for this combination in these indications and enables forthcoming safety and activity readouts.
catalyst_text_evidence: Tango Therapeutics, Inc. (NASDAQ: TNGX) ... and Erasca, Inc. (Nasdaq: ERAS) ... today announced that the Phase 1/2 study of oral PRMT5 inhibitor vopimetostat in combination with pan-RAS molecular glue ERAS-0015 in patients with MTAP-deleted pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) and MTAP-deleted/RAS-mutant non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) is now open for enrollment.

drug_indication: Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma, Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer
catalyst_text: Phase 1/2 trial initiated and open for enrollment
detailed_catalyst_text: An open-label Phase 1/2 dose-escalation and expansion study evaluating a PRMT5 inhibitor with ERAS-0015 in MTAP-deleted pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma and MTAP-deleted/RAS-mutant non-small cell lung cancer is now open for enrollment. The trial’s dose-escalation primary objective is to determine the maximum tolerated dose, with secondary objectives assessing antitumor activity, pharmacokinetics, safety, and tolerability. This marks the initiation of combination development for ERAS-0015 across pancreatic and lung cancer settings.
catalyst_text_evidence: BOSTON and SAN DIEGO, 2026-11-04 ... today announced that the Phase 1/2 study of oral PRMT5 inhibitor vopimetostat in combination with pan-RAS molecular glue ERAS-0015 in patients with MTAP-deleted pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) and MTAP-deleted/RAS-mutant non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) is now open for enrollment. The Phase 1/2 open-label, multicenter dose-escalation and expansion trial, sponsored by Tango Therapeutics, is designed to evaluate vopimetostat in combination with ERAS-0015 in patients with MTAP-deleted PDAC or RAS-mutant/MTAP-deleted NSCLC. The primary objective of the dose-escalation portion of the study is to determine the maximum tolerated dose of the combination regimen. Secondary objectives include assessment of antitumor activity, pharmacokinetics, safety and tolerability.

catalyst_text: Reported strong Phase 1 responses plus Fast Track
detailed_catalyst_text: The press release recaps preliminary Phase 1 monotherapy results in PDAC showing notable unconfirmed response rates in second-line KRAS G12X patients, alongside favorable early tolerability. It also notes the drug received FDA Fast Track designation for metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma on 2026-08-24, supporting expedited development.
catalyst_text_evidence: The analysis follows FDA approval of Revolution Medicines’ daraxonrasib in pretreated metastatic PDAC in August 2026 and FDA Fast Track designation for ERAS-0015 in metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma on 2026-08-24. Preliminary Phase 1 monotherapy data from the U.S. AURORAS-1 trial and the China JYP0015M101 study have shown: Unconfirmed overall response rates (uORR) of 40% at pharmacologically active doses of 16–32 mg once daily and 42% at recommended expansion doses of 24–32 mg in second-line KRAS G12X PDAC. A July 2026 update reporting a 57% unconfirmed 8-week ORR at the 32 mg once-daily recommended expansion dose in second-line or later KRAS G12X PDAC. Generally favorable early tolerability, with mostly low-grade treatment-related adverse events, no dose-limiting toxicities at disclosed cutoffs, and 100% median relative dose intensity at 24 mg and 32 mg once daily.

catalyst_text: Received FDA Fast Track designation for indication
detailed_catalyst_text: The FDA granted Fast Track Designation to ERAS-0015 for the treatment of metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma. This regulatory designation can expedite development and review for a serious condition with high unmet need and was supported by early clinical activity.
catalyst_text_evidence: SAN DIEGO, 2026-08-24 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Erasca, Inc. (Nasdaq: ERAS)... today announced that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has granted Fast Track Designation (FTD) to ERAS-0015 for the treatment of patients with metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma.

catalyst_text: Reported favorable Phase 1 combination safety and progress
detailed_catalyst_text: In metastatic colorectal cancer, the Phase 1 combination with panitumumab showed no DLTs in the 16 mg cohort and cleared the first dose escalation cohort. These safety findings indicate encouraging tolerability for the combination and supported continued enrollment and dose escalation.
catalyst_text_evidence: Promising Combination Potential with Panitumumab in Metastatic Colorectal Cancer (CRC), including Clearance of First Dose Escalation Cohort. No DLTs were observed for the combination in the 16 mg cohort during dose escalation in four DLT-evaluable patients. Backfill enrollment is ongoing in the 16 mg combination cohort. Dose escalation is ongoing with continued enrollment in the 24 mg combination cohort. DCO 2026-07-06.

catalyst_text: Posted positive Phase 1 data with strong responses
detailed_catalyst_text: Updated preliminary Phase 1 results showed a 57% uORR at the recommended expansion dose of 32 mg QD in second-line or later KRAS G12X pancreatic cancer. Safety remained favorable with mostly low-grade TRAEs, no DLTs, and a median relative dose intensity of 100% at 24 mg and 32 mg. These findings demonstrate encouraging monotherapy activity and tolerability supporting continued development.
catalyst_text_evidence: SAN DIEGO, 2026-07-13 ... today announced updated preliminary Phase 1 data for its potentially best-in-class, pan-RAS molecular glue ERAS-0015 in patients with RAS-mutant solid tumors. Encouraging Monotherapy Responses Observed in Second Line or Greater (2L+) KRAS G12X Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma (PDAC) 57% uORR8wk (N=7) at recommended dose for expansion (RDE) of 32 mg QD. With Additional Patients and Longer Follow-up, Monotherapy Safety Data Remained Consistent with Prior Disclosure and ERAS-0015 Continued to be Generally Well-Tolerated. Mostly low-grade TRAEs, no dose-limiting toxicities (DLTs), low rate of dose interruptions or reductions due to TRAEs, and no discontinuations due to TRAEs. Median relative dose intensity (RDI) was 100% at both 24 mg QD and 32 mg QD. Data cutoff (DCO) 2026-05-25.

catalyst_text: Reported positive preliminary Phase 1 dose escalation results
detailed_catalyst_text: Preliminary Phase 1 dose escalation results from the AURORAS-1 trial in RAS-mutant solid tumors showed favorable safety and tolerability, linear pharmacokinetics, and both confirmed and unconfirmed partial responses across multiple tumor types. Early activity observed at doses as low as 8 mg once daily supports continued clinical development and potential best-in-class differentiation.
catalyst_text_evidence: Erasca is evaluating ERAS-0015 in the AURORAS-1 Phase 1 trial in patients with RAS-mutant solid tumors. Early dose escalation data in AURORAS-1 demonstrated favorable safety and tolerability results, well-behaved, linear PK, and confirmed and unconfirmed partial responses in multiple patients across multiple tumor types with different RAS mutations, including confirmed and unconfirmed partial responses at doses as low as 8 mg once daily (QD).

catalyst_text: Reported positive preliminary Phase 1 dose escalation results
detailed_catalyst_text: Preliminary Phase 1 monotherapy data in second-line KRAS G12X pancreatic cancer showed uORR of 40% at 16–32 mg QD and 42% at 24–32 mg QD, with 50% uORR at 32 mg QD. These results indicate meaningful activity in a hard-to-treat population.
catalyst_text_evidence: PDAC At PADs of 16-32 mg QD, 40% uORR14wk (N=20) in 2L KRAS G12X PDAC, which exceeded comparator by 11 percentage points5,6 At RDEs of 24-32 mg QD, 42% uORR14wk (N=12) in 2L KRAS G12X PDAC, which exceeded comparator by 13 percentage points5,6 At RDE of 32 mg QD, 50% uORR14wk (N=2) in 2L KRAS G12X PDAC, which exceeded comparator by 15 percentage points5,7

drug_indication: KRAS G12X Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer
catalyst_text: Reported positive preliminary Phase 1 dose escalation results
detailed_catalyst_text: Preliminary Phase 1 monotherapy results in KRAS G12X NSCLC showed strong activity, including uORR of 62% in 2L+ and 75% in post-ICI/platinum cohorts at 16–32 mg QD, and 64% uORR at 24–32 mg QD. Safety was generally well-tolerated with mostly low-grade adverse events and no dose-limiting toxicities reported to date.
catalyst_text_evidence: Efficacy: Robust monotherapy overall response rates (ORR) in patients with KRAS G12X non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) and with KRAS G12X pancreatic cancer (PDAC), in each case as of the relevant data cutoff (DCO)1,2: NSCLC At PADs of 16-32 mg QD, 62% uORR8wk (N=37) in second line or greater (2L+) KRAS G12X NSCLC, which exceeded comparator by 24 percentage points3,4 At PADs of 16-32 mg QD, 75% uORR8wk (N=16) in post-ICI/platinum (2/3L) KRAS G12X NSCLC, which exceeded comparator by 37 percentage points3,4 At recommended doses for expansion (RDEs) of 24-32 mg QD, 64% uORR8wk (N=25) in 2L+ KRAS G12X NSCLC3 Safety and Tolerability: Generally well-tolerated with mostly low-grade adverse events (AEs), no dose-limiting toxicities (DLTs), low rate of dose interruptions or reductions due to treatment-related adverse events (TRAEs), and no discontinuations due to TRAEs

catalyst_text: Reported encouraging Phase 1 combination dose escalation data
detailed_catalyst_text: Early Phase 1 combination data with panitumumab in metastatic colorectal cancer showed no DLTs in N=3 and an unconfirmed partial response in the efficacy-evaluable patient. These findings support the feasibility of combining with standard-of-care anti-EGFR therapy.
catalyst_text_evidence: Preliminary data suggest ERAS-0015 may combine safely with standard-of-care doses of panitumumab with no DLTs as of DCO (N=3) and 1/1 uPR in CRC Combinability: ERAS-0015 showed promising clinical potential to combine with panitumumab (anti-EGFR monoclonal antibody) No DLTs observed through the 2026-03-31 DCO (N=3) with 1 unconfirmed partial response (uPR) in 1 efficacy-evaluable patient with metastatic colorectal cancer (CRC)

catalyst_text: Initiated Phase 1 monotherapy expansion and combination cohorts
detailed_catalyst_text: Monotherapy expansion and combination dose escalation cohorts in the U.S. Phase 1 program were initiated. Starting these cohorts ahead of prior guidance advances clinical development and broadens safety and efficacy assessment across tumor types.
catalyst_text_evidence: Key Upcoming and Completed Milestones The Company initiated ERAS-0015 monotherapy expansion and combination dose escalation cohorts in the US (in Q2 2026 and Q1 2026, respectively), both ahead of previous guidance.
